\mxunit{automatismes-ch03}{Real numbers and intervals}

\begin{fluencysheet}{Thu~19~Nov.~2026}{Sets of numbers: $\N,\Z,\D,\Q,\R$}
\mxfq{Warm-up · Quick}{NUM}{Give the decimal form of $\dfrac38$ and an approximation of $\dfrac56$ to within $10^{-3}$.}{$\num{0,375}$; $\num{0,833}$.}{}
\mxfq{Core · Method}{NUM}{Give the smallest set ($\N,\Z,\D,\Q,\R$) containing each of these numbers: $-4$; $\num{0,25}$; $\dfrac13$; $\sqrt2$; $\dfrac63$.}{$-4\in\Z$; $\num{0,25}\in\D$; $\dfrac13\in\Q$; $\sqrt2\in\R$; $\dfrac63=2\in\N$.}{The smallest set is the key: $\dfrac63$ is a natural number.}
\mxfq{Core + · True/false}{NUM}{True or false? Justify. The number $\dfrac13$ is a decimal number.}{False. If there were integers $a$ and $n$ with $\dfrac13=\dfrac{a}{10^n}$, then $10^n=3a$ would be divisible by $3$: impossible (the sum of the digits of $10^n$ is $1$).}{}
\mxfq{Review · Quick}{SUB}{Calculate $(x+1)(x-3)$ for $x=2$.}{$-3$.}{}
\mxfq{Thread · Quick}{SOL}{How many faces, vertices and edges does a right triangular prism have?}{$5$ faces ($2$ triangles, $3$ rectangles), $6$ vertices, $9$ edges.}{}
\end{fluencysheet}

\begin{fluencysheet}{Mon~23~Nov.~2026}{Decimal bounds and rounding}
\mxfq{Warm-up · Quick}{NUM}{Round $\num{3,14159}$ to the nearest $10^{-2}$ and then to the nearest $10^{-3}$.}{$\num{3,14}$ then $\num{3,142}$.}{The next digit decides: $1<5$ then $5\geqslant5$.}
\mxfq{Core · Method}{NUM}{Bound $\sqrt2$ between two decimals that differ by $10^{-2}$.}{$\num{1,41}^2=\num{1,9881}<2<\num{2,0164}=\num{1,42}^2$: $\num{1,41}<\sqrt2<\num{1,42}$.}{}
\mxfq{Core + · Code reading}{ALG}{What is the final value of \code{k}? What can be deduced about $\sqrt2$?\mxpseudo{k = 10\\ while (k/10)**2 \textless{} 2:\\ \mxtab k = k + 1}}{$k=15$: $\num{1,4}^2=\num{1,96}<2$ and $\num{1,5}^2=\num{2,25}\geqslant2$, so $\num{1,4}<\sqrt2\leqslant\num{1,5}$.}{}
\mxfq{Review · Quick}{QP}{$5$ kg of rice cost $\num{12500}$ Ar. How much do $8$ kg cost?}{$\dfrac{\num{12500}}{5}\times8=\num{20000}$ Ar.}{}
\mxfq{Thread · True/false}{DEM}{True or false? Justify. A quadrilateral whose diagonals have equal length is a rectangle.}{False. Counter-example: an isosceles trapezium has diagonals of equal length without being a rectangle.}{}
\end{fluencysheet}

\begin{fluencysheet}{Tue~24~Nov.~2026}{Irrational numbers: $\frac13$ is not decimal, $\sqrt2$ is irrational}
\mxfq{Warm-up · Quick}{CAL}{Write $\sqrt{12}$ and $\sqrt{50}$ in the form $a\sqrt b$ with $b$ the smallest possible integer.}{$\sqrt{12}=2\sqrt3$; $\sqrt{50}=5\sqrt2$.}{}
\mxfq{Core · Sorting}{NUM}{Among $\num{0,333}\ldots$; $\sqrt9$; $\sqrt2$; $\pi$; $\dfrac{22}{7}$, which are rational?}{$\num{0,333}\ldots=\dfrac13$; $\sqrt9=3$; $\dfrac{22}7$: rational. $\sqrt2$ and $\pi$ are irrational.}{$\dfrac{22}{7}$ is only an approximation of $\pi$, not equal to $\pi$.}
\mxfq{Core + · Reasoning}{DEM}{Suppose $\sqrt2=\dfrac pq$ with $\dfrac pq$ in lowest terms, so $p^2=2q^2$. What can be said about the parity of $p$, then of $q$? What contradiction arises?}{$p^2$ even, so $p$ even, $p=2k$; then $4k^2=2q^2$, $q^2=2k^2$: $q$ even. Contradiction with the fraction being in lowest terms.}{}
\mxfq{Review · Table}{STA}{Values $1\,;\,2\,;\,3\,;\,4$ with frequencies $5\,;\,8\,;\,4\,;\,3$. Give the total frequency, the relative frequency of the value $2$ and the mean.\par\smallskip\mxarraystretch{1.15}\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline
Value & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ \hline
Frequency & 5 & 8 & 4 & 3 \\ \hline
\end{tabular}\par }{Total $20$; relative frequency $\dfrac{8}{20}=\pc{40}$; mean $\dfrac{5+16+12+12}{20}=\num{2,25}$.}{}
\mxfq{Thread · Quick}{REP}{Give the coordinates of the reflection of $A\pt{3;-2}$ in the y-axis.}{$\pt{-3;-2}$.}{Pitfall: changing the sign of the ordinate (reflection in the x-axis).}

\begin{fluencysheet}{Thu~26~Nov.~2026}{Intervals of $\R$: notation and representation}
\mxfq{Warm-up · Quick}{CMP}{Compare $-3$ and $-5$, then $-\dfrac12$ and $-\num{0,6}$.}{$-3>-5$; $-\num{0,5}>-\num{0,6}$.}{For negative numbers, the one with the smaller absolute value is the greater.}
\mxfq{Core · Method}{NUM}{Write as an interval: $-2\leqslant x<5$; $x>3$; $x\leqslant0$.}{$\intfo{-2}{5}$; $\intoo{3}{+\infty}$; $\intof{-\infty}{0}$.}{The bracket faces inwards if the endpoint is included; $\infty$ is always excluded.}
\mxfq{Core + · MCQ}{NUM}{The intersection $\intoo{-\infty}{2}\,\cap\,\intff{-1}{4}$ is:\mxchoices{$\intof{2}{4}$}{$\intof{-\infty}{4}$}{$\intfo{-1}{2}$}{$\intff{-1}{2}$}}{C.\ $\intfo{-1}{2}$}{Intersection: values satisfying both conditions $x<2$ and $-1\leqslant x\leqslant4$.}
\mxfq{Review · Table}{LEC}{Journey times (min).\par\smallskip\mxarraystretch{1.15}\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline
Class & $\intfo{0}{10}$ & $\intfo{10}{20}$ & $\intfo{20}{30}$ \\ \hline
Frequency & 4 & 9 & 7 \\ \hline
\end{tabular}\par What are the total frequency, the modal class and the relative frequency of $\intfo{10}{20}$?}{$20$; $\intfo{10}{20}$; $\dfrac{9}{20}=\pc{45}$.}{}
\mxfq{Thread · Problem}{DIV}{One bus runs every $15$ min, another every $20$ min. They are together at $8$ a.m. At what time are they next together?}{$\ppcm\pt{15;20}=60$: at $9$ a.m.}{}
\end{fluencysheet}

\begin{fluencysheet}{Mon~30~Nov.~2026}{Absolute value and distance between two real numbers}
\mxfq{Warm-up · Quick}{REP}{What is the distance between $-3$ and $5$ on the number line?}{$|5-(-3)|=8$.}{}
\mxfq{Core · Quick}{CAL}{Calculate $|{-}7|$, $|3-8|$ and $|\pi-4|$.}{$7$; $5$; $|\pi-4|=4-\pi$ since $\pi<4$.}{}
\mxfq{Core + · Method}{EQ}{Solve $|x-3|=2$.}{The real numbers at distance $2$ from $3$: $x=1$ or $x=5$.}{Geometric interpretation rather than case by case.}
\mxfq{Review · Formula}{IMG}{$f(x)=x^2-3$. Give the image of $-2$ and the preimages of $6$.}{$f(-2)=1$; $x^2-3=6\Leftrightarrow x^2=9$: preimages $-3$ and $3$.}{}
\mxfq{Thread · Formula → table}{REG}{$f(x)=-x+3$. Complete: $f(-1)$, $f(0)$, $f(2)$.}{$4\ ;\ 3\ ;\ 1$.}{}
\end{fluencysheet}

\begin{fluencysheet}{Tue~1\textsuperscript{st}~Dec.~2026}{Inequality $|x-a|\leqslant r$ and the associated interval}
\mxfq{Warm-up · Quick}{EQ}{Solve $2x-3\leqslant5$.}{$2x\leqslant8$, $x\leqslant4$: $S=\intof{-\infty}{4}$.}{}
\mxfq{Core · Method}{EQ}{Solve $|x-2|\leqslant3$ and give $S$ as an interval.}{The real numbers at distance at most $3$ from $2$: $S=\intff{-1}{5}$.}{Check: $|{-}1-2|=3$ and $|5-2|=3$.}
\mxfq{Core + · Translate}{NUM}{Express as an inequality with absolute value: $x\in\intff{-1}{5}$ then $x\in\intoo{4}{10}$.}{$|x-2|\leqslant3$ (centre $2$, radius $3$); $|x-7|<3$ (centre $7$, radius $3$).}{}
